questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\left[t\right]$ denote the greatest integer $\le t$. If $\lambdaεR - \left\{0, 1\right\}, \lim_{x \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - x + \left|x\right|}{\lambda - x + \left[x\right]}\right| = L$, then $L$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - x + \left|x\right|}{\lambda - x + \left[x\right]}\right| = L$

Let's find left-hand and right-hand limit.

For left-hand limit

$x = 0 - h, x \to 0, h \to 0, h > 0$

$LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - \left(- h\right) + \left|- h\right|}{\lambda - \left(- h\right) + \left[- h\right]}\right|$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h - \left(- h\right)}{\lambda + h + \left[- h\right]}\right|$

Since $h > 0 ⇒ \left[- h\right] = - 1$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h + h}{\lambda + h - 1}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda - 1\right|}$

For right-hand limit

$x = 0 + h, x \to 0, h \to 0, h > 0$

$RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - h + \left|h\right|}{\lambda - h + \left[h\right]}\right|$

Since $h > 0 ⇒ \left[h\right] = 0$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h + h}{\lambda + h + 0}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda\right|}$

For existence of limit $LHL = RHL$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda - 1\right|} = \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda\right|}$

Cross multiply and square both side.

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = {\left(\lambda - 1\right)}^{2} ⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = {\lambda}^{2} + 1 - 2\lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Limit $L = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2$

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\left\{\dfrac{1}{{x}^{8}}\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4}\right)\right\} = {2}^{- k}$ then the value of k is
questions.solution:

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4}\right)}{{x}^{8}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}{{x}^{4}} \times \dfrac{\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4}\right)}{{x}^{4}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}{4 \times \left(\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4}\right)} \times \dfrac{\left(1 - cos\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4}\right)}{16 \times \left(\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{16}\right)}$

Using $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 - cosx}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{1}{256} = {2}^{- 8}$

$⇒ {2}^{- 8} = {2}^{- k} ⇒ k = 8$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{{x}^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1} = 5,$ then $a + b$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $L = \lim_{x \to 1} ⁡ \dfrac{{x}^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1} = 5$

As $x \to 1,$ the denominator becomes zero, hence for finite limit, the numerator must also approach to zero as $x \to 1$

$⇒ 1 - a + b = 0$

$⇒ b = a - 1 \ldots ( 1 )$

Now $L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{{x}^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1}$\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right)$ form

By using L'Hospital Rule,

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{2x - a}{1}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{2x - a}{1} = 5$

$⇒ 2 - a = 5 ⇒ a = - 3$

From the equation $\left(1\right),$ we get

$⇒ b = a - 1 = - 4$

$⇒ a + b = - 7 .$

questions.q: If $f\left(x\right) = \left[x\right] - \left[\dfrac{x}{4}\right], x \in R,$ where $\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer function, then:
options: Both $\lim_{x \to 4 -}f\left(x\right)$ and $\lim_{x \to 4 +}f\left(x\right)$ exist but are not equal
questions.solution:
$R . H . L . = \lim_{x \to {4}^{+}}\left[x\right] - \left[\dfrac{x}{4}\right] = 4 - 1 = 3$

$L . H . L . = \lim_{x \to {4}^{-}}\left[x\right] - \left[\dfrac{x}{4}\right] = 3 - 0 = 3$

$f\left(x\right) = 4 - 1 = 3$

$L . H . L . = f\left(4\right) = R . H . L .$

Hence, given function is continuous at $x = 4 .$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}}\dfrac{\pi - 2\sin^{- 1}x}{\sqrt{1 - x}\left(\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1}x}\right)} = \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}}\dfrac{2\cos^{- 1}x}{\sqrt{1 - x}\left(\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1}x}\right)}$

Let $K = \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}x}{\sqrt{1 - x}}$ and put $x = cos\theta$, we get

$K = \lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{\theta}{2} . 2}{\sqrt{2} . sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}} = \lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\dfrac{sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}}{\dfrac{\theta}{2}}} = \sqrt{2}\left[∵ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx}{x} = 1\right]$

$∴ L = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{\pi}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{\pi}}$.

Let $[\mathrm{x}]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $\mathrm{X}$. Then :

$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(|\mathrm{x}|-\sin (x[x]))^{2}}{x^{2}}$
questions.solution:
RHL is, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(x-0)^{2}}{x^{2}}$=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right.}{x^{2}}+1\right)=1+\pi$

And LHL is, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(-x+\sin x)^{2}}{x^{2}}$=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+x^{2}+\sin ^{2} x-2 x \sin x}{x^{2}}$=\pi+1+1-2=\pi$

Since, LHL $\neq$ RHL Hence, limit does not exist.

RHL is, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(x-0)^{2}}{x^{2}}$=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right.}{x^{2}}+1\right)=1+\pi$

And LHL is, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(-x+\sin x)^{2}}{x^{2}}$=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+x^{2}+\sin ^{2} x-2 x \sin x}{x^{2}}$=\pi+1+1-2=\pi$

Since, LHL $\neq$ RHL Hence, limit does not exist.

$\lim_{x \to {1}^{+}}\dfrac{\left(1 - \left|x\right| + sin\left|1 - x\right|\right)sin\left(\left[1 - x\right]\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{\left|1 - x\right|\left[1 - x\right]}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - \left|\left(1 + h\right)\right| + sin\left|1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right|\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\left[1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right]\right)}{\left|1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right|\left[1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right]}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - h - 1 + sin\left|\left(1 - h - 1\right)\right|\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\left[1 - 1 - h\right]\right)}{\left|\left(1 - 1 - h\right)\right|\left[1 - 1 - h\right]}$

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{{y}^{4}}$
questions.solution:
To solve this question, we need to apply the concept of rationalization twice.

Given limit is $\lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{{y}^{4}} ( \dfrac{0}{0}form )$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{{y}^{4}} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}} - 1\right)}{{y}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)} \times \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}} + 1\right)}{\left(\sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{{y}^{4}}{{y}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{1}{\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{1 + {y}^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x \tan 2 x-2 x \tan x}{(1-\cos 2 x)^2}$ equals.
questions.solution:
Let,

$\begin{aligned}$&L=$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{(x \tan 2 x-2 x \tan x)}{(1-\cos 2 x)^2}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}$K $\text{ (say) }$\\
&\Rightarrow K=$\frac{x\left[\frac{2 \tan x}{1-(\tan x)^2}\right]-2 x \tan x}{\left(1-\left(1-2 \sin ^2 x\right)\right)^2}$\\
&=$\frac{2 x \tan x-\left[2 x \tan x-2 x \tan ^3 x\right]}{4 \sin ^4 x \times\left(1-\tan ^2 x\right)}$\\
&=$\frac{2 x \tan ^3 x}{4 \sin ^4 x \times\left(1-\tan ^2 x\right)}$\\
&=$\frac{2 x \tan ^3 x}{4 \sin ^4 x \times\left(\frac{\cos ^2 x-\sin ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x}\right)}
\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}$&=$\frac{2 x \frac{\sin ^3 x}{\cos ^3 x}}{4 \sin ^4 x \times\left(\frac{\cos ^2 x-\sin ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x}\right)}$\\
& \Rightarrow K=$\frac{x}{2 \sin x \times\left(\cos ^2 x-\sin ^2 x\right) \cos x}$\\
\therefore L &=$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x}{2 \sin x} \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{\cos x\left(\cos ^2 x-\sin ^2 x\right)}$\\
&=$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x}{2 \sin x} \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{\cos 0\left(\cos ^2 0-\sin ^2 0\right)}$\\
&=$\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: For each $t \in R,$ let $\left[t\right]$ be the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}x\left(\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right] + \left[\dfrac{2}{x}\right] + \ldots + \left[\dfrac{15}{x}\right]\right)$
questions.solution:
We know that

$\dfrac{1}{x} - 1 < \left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right] \le \dfrac{1}{x}$

Hence,

$\dfrac{1 + 2 + 3 . . . + 15}{x} - 15 < \left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right] + \left[\dfrac{2}{x}\right] + .... + \left[\dfrac{15}{x}\right] \le \dfrac{1 + 2 + ... + 15}{x}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}x\left(\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right] + \left[\dfrac{2}{x}\right] + . ... + \left[\dfrac{15}{x}\right]\right) = 15\left(\dfrac{16}{2}\right)$

$= 120$

questions.q: If $f\left(x\right)$ is a differentiable function in the interval $\left(0, \infty\right)$ such that $f\left(1\right) = 1$ and $\lim_{t \to x} ⁡ \dfrac{{t}^{2}f\left(x\right) - {x}^{2}f\left(t\right)}{t - x} = 1,$for each $x > 0,$ then $f\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $L = \lim_{t \to x} ⁡ \dfrac{{t}^{2}f\left(x\right) - {x}^{2}f\left(t\right)}{t - x} = 1$

Applying L'Hospital Rule

$L = \lim_{t \to x} ⁡ \dfrac{2tf\left(x\right) - {x}^{2}{f}^{′}\left(t\right)}{1} = 1$

Or $2xf\left(x\right) - {x}^{2}{f}^{′}\left(x\right) = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- \dfrac{2}{x}\right)y = - \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}$..........$( 1 )$

Solving the above linear differential equation we get

Integrating factor $= {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = {e}^{- 2lnx} = \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}$

After multiplying the equation $\left(1\right)$ by $\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}$, and simplifying the equation $\left(1\right)$ becomes,

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{{x}^{2}}\right) = - \dfrac{1}{{x}^{4}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{{x}^{2}} = ∫ - \dfrac{1}{{x}^{4}}dx = \dfrac{1}{3{x}^{3}} + c$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{3x} + c{x}^{2}$

Putting $x = 1, y = 1$, we get

$c = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

$∴ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}{x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3x}$

Put $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$f\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} \times {\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{2}{3 \times 3}$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{27 + 4}{18} = \dfrac{31}{18}$.

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)\left(n + 2\right) \ldots . 3n}{{n}^{2n}}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
\left(n + 1\right)\left(n + 2\right) \ldots . \left(n + 2n\right)}{{n}^{2n}}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}$

$y = \left(\dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)}{n} \cdot \dfrac{\left(n + 2\right)}{n} \ldots \ldots \dfrac{\left(n + 2n\right)}{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}$

$logy = \dfrac{1}{n}\left[log\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) + log\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{n}\right) + \ldots . . log\left(1 + \dfrac{2n}{n}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{n}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{2n}ln\left(1 + r / n\right)$

Replace $∑ \to ∫$ & $\dfrac{r}{n} \to x$ & $\dfrac{1}{n} \to dx$

As $n \to \infty$

$logy = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}log\left(1 + x\right)dx$

Integrating by parts, we get,

$logy = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}1 \cdot log\left(1 + x\right)dx$

$= {\left(x \cdot log\left(1 + x\right)\right)}_{0}^{2} - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{1}{1 + x}xdx$

$= {\left(xlog\left(1 + x\right)\right)}_{0}^{2} - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 + x}\right)dx + \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{1}{1 + x}dx$

$= {\left(xlog\left(1 + x\right)\right)}_{0}^{2} - {\left(x\right)}_{0}^{2} + {\left(log\left(1 + x\right)\right)}_{0}^{2}$

$= \left(2log3 - 0\right) - \left(2 - 0\right) + \left(log3 - log1\right)$

$= 3log3 - 2$

Since $logy = 3log3 - 2 = log27 - log{e}^{2}$

$= y = \dfrac{{e}^{log27}}{{e}^{2}} = \dfrac{27}{{e}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{27}{{e}^{2}}$.

$P = e\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan \left(x-2\left\{x^2+k+2 x-2 k\right\}\right.}{x^2-4 x+4}=5$, then $\mathrm{k}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}$& $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan (x-2)\left\{x^2+(k-2) x-2 k\right\}}{x^2-4 x+4}=$5 \\
\Rightarrow & $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan (x-2)\left\{x^2+k x-2 x-2 k\right\}}{(x-2)^2}=$5 \\
\Rightarrow & $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan (x-2)\{x(x-2)+k(x-2)\}}{(x-2) \times(x-2)}=$5 \\
\Rightarrow $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2}\left(\frac{\tan (x-2)}{(x-2)}\right) \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 2}\left(\frac{(k+x)(x-2)}{(x-2)}\right)=$5 \\
\Rightarrow & 1 $\times \lim _{x \rightarrow 2}($k+x)=5 \\
&$\left$\{\because $\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tan h}{h}=$1\right\} \\
& $\text{ or }$k+2=5 \\
\Rightarrow k=3
\end{aligned}
questions.question: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan \left(x-2\left\{x^2+k+2 x-2 k\right\}\right.}{x^2-4 x+4}=5$, then $\mathrm{k}$ is equal to:

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ } & \lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan (x-2)\left\{x^2+(k-2) x-2 k\right\}}{x^2-4 x+4}=5 \\
\Rightarrow & \lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan (x-2)\left\{x^2+k x-2 x-2 k\right\}}{(x-2)^2}=5 \\
\Rightarrow & \lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\tan (x-2)\{x(x-2)+k(x-2)\}}{(x-2) \times(x-2)}=5 \\
\Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 2}\left(\frac{\tan (x-2)}{(x-2)}\right) \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 2}\left(\frac{(k+x)(x-2)}{(x-2)}\right)=5 \\
\Rightarrow & 1 \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 2}(k+x)=5 \\
&\left\{\because \lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tan h}{h}=1\right\} \\
& \text{ or } k+2=5 \\
\Rightarrow k=3
\end{aligned}
$

\end{aligned}

By sandwich theorem.

\Rightarrow $\lim _{x \rightarrow$ \infty} $\frac{f(2 x)}{f(x)}=$1
